cōnsilium, cōnsiliī n.

noun, second declension

a council; a committee

Counsel, and then the body that gives it: a general’s council, the elders of Carthage (see council, an advisory body). Morgan–Owens gives it for a committee, and cōnsilium ex utrāque factiōne collēctum for a panel drawn from both parties (s.v. bipartisan). A Roman board was named by its number: trēsvirī, decemvirī.

Other words

  • concilium, conciliī n. — an assembly; Traupman’s word for a committee

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Traupman 178, 294

    Classically an assembly called to take counsel (see council, an advisory body).

Examples

  • cōnsilium ex utrāque factiōne collēctum

    a committee drawn from both partiesM-O s.v. bipartisan

See also council, meeting, organization, council.
